title: The Cut and the Puppet Master
subtitle: In Which The Building Meets The One Word It Cannot Argue With, And Waluigi Meets The Man Holding The Off Switch
standfirst: The sequel to the promo account arrived the same night it was corrected, because this studio does not close. A coffee machine that was not an exit, a brother found alive at a blue light, a villain who fights to the music, one word that stops the whole building, applause for an empty room — and, at the end of a dark hallway, a small wired remote. Waluigi is going to talk through every second of it. He has NOT slept. WAH.
pullQuote: The applause was for NOBODY. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.
filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — the teaser, the correction, and the sequel, all in one day, because this file does not respect mealtimes

sections.heading: The Sequel Arrives The Same Night, Because This Studio Has Never Heard Of A Credits Roll
sections.body:
Some context first, filed gently, because Waluigi has learned things about this building in the last twelve hours and NONE of them are calming.

This morning Waluigi filed a newspaper clipping as a review. This evening the full account arrived, proved the clipping was a trailer, and Waluigi filed the correction with his teeth gritted and a promise in print that the archive would not let that happen twice. And then the SAME EVENING produced a sequel. Not the next day. Not after a rest. The new account picks up in the break room minutes after the old one ended, which means somewhere in that world a television studio looked at two shell-shocked nobles, one missing plumber, and a producer shaped like a Wario, and said: MORE. Waluigi has been in this business long enough to know what MORE means. It means a sequel, and it means Waluigi works tonight.

So here is the commentary track for the sequel, and Waluigi is going to talk through ALL of it, because the parts that look like an escape story are actually a management chart wearing an escape story as a costume, and somebody in this archive has to say so in a loud voice. That somebody is Waluigi. It is always Waluigi. I have checked the roster and there is nobody else on it.

Where we left them: Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores and his steward, Alistair of the Marshkeepers, sealed in the employee break room of the *Nintendo Mania* studio. Four monitors showing static. One monitor showing a lie. The coffee machine gone cold. And through the walls, the sound of a corrupted Mario beating the real one somewhere out in the corridors — which is the single worst piece of ambient noise Waluigi has filed all year, and Waluigi once filed an event with SCREAMING FURNITURE.

How do we get out of here, though. We have no other leads but this place. That is the sentence the account opens on, and Waluigi wants it on the record that the lord of the Dark Shores said LEADS, plural, about a coffee machine and five monitors, and he was CORRECT, because in this building a coffee machine is a lead. Alistair surveyed the room like the steward he is — back door to the kitchen, air vent big enough to crawl through, monitors showing possible exits — and then found the thing that was new.

A small button by the coffee machine. Labelled EMERGENCY EXIT.

Waluigi has filed entire investigations that began with less. Hold that button in your mind. It is about to be the most honest and the most dishonest object in this whole filing, and it is both AT THE SAME TIME, which in this studio counts as a personality. Waluigi has met appliances with worse ethics.

sections.heading: The Button Said EXIT, The Machine Said Coffee, And The Ceiling Said You're Welcome
sections.body:
Darian pressed the button with, and the account is precise about this, the specific pessimism of a man testing whether the exit is another trap. *Brilliant, let's see how it's not an exit to the coffee machine.* Waluigi has read that sentence four times and respects it more with each pass. That is not cynicism. That is CALIBRATION. Two filings in this building will do that to a man, and Darian has had both of them in a single day.

The coffee machine came to life. Aggressively. Scalding coffee poured out uncontrollably, the room filled with steam, and Alistair coughed out the sentence *it's… not an exit* — and Waluigi is going to stop him right there, because the steward was WRONG, and being wrong in exactly the right direction is the theme of this entire session.

The steam rose. Steam does that. And a ceiling vent popped open from the heat.

Sit with the mechanics of it. The button did not open a door. The button made coffee. The coffee made steam. The steam opened the exit. The building hid an escape route behind an appliance, or the appliance staged a rescue, and Waluigi filed the line in the account and he stands behind every word of it: in this studio those are the same sentence with different fonts. The archive has a shelf now for lying exits. The shelf is getting FULL. Waluigi labeled the shelf himself, and the studio keeps stocking it.

Then the men armed themselves, and the armory was the break room, and Waluigi wants the arsenal read out slowly because it is the most provincial loadout ever carried into a television studio: Darian took a heavy metal rolling pin, and the broken coffee-pot handle with its sharp edge. A rolling pin. A SHARD OF COFFEE POT. Somewhere in the Dark Shores, Waluigi is certain, an armory master felt a disturbance and does not know why.

Alistair shut off the machine before they climbed — the steward turns OFF what the lord turns ON, which is either a marriage or a checks-and-balances system — Waluigi has worked in institutions, and that arrangement is called GOVERNANCE — — the steam cleared, and he boosted his lord up into the duct first.

The steward boosted the king. Waluigi wants that remembered. Not the other way round. The lord goes UP into the dark ceiling of an alien building first, on his steward's hands, holding a rolling pin. Waluigi has filed kings who would not carry their own map. This one goes into the duct FIRST, and the account does not even pause to be proud of it, which is how you know it is habit. Waluigi notices habits. Habits are character, filed under pressure.

sections.heading: The Exit Is Up, The Rat Is Honest, And The Steward Says The Sentence Of The Year
sections.body:
The vent was dark, dusty, cramped. Hands and knees. Faint emergency light from below, small cracks letting in glow. Something scurried past Darian's face.

A rat. An ordinary rat.

And Waluigi confesses he UNDERSTOOD the account at that moment, because the account says the rat was almost reassuring — after the black-eyed thing on Camera Three in the previous filing, an ordinary rat reads like a courtesy. This building has reset Waluigi's standards so thoroughly that VERMIN now scores as HOSPITALITY. Waluigi is filing that about himself honestly, because a commentator who cannot admit his benchmarks have moved is just a narrator with better fonts. The archive has standards. Waluigi simply cannot find them this week.

Then Darian fumbled for the rolling pin, and the metal clanged against the duct walls, and the clang became one long echo rolling through the entire system, and Waluigi would like the acoustics noted: the building heard EVERYTHING. Every duct is a microphone. Every crawl is a broadcast. The studio that lies about exits is perfectly honest about eavesdropping.

And Alistair whispered the sentence this archive would like bronzed and mounted over the door: *careful — noise might draw attention.*

The steward. Whispering. To the king. About noise. In a building where the walls applaud on command. It is the single most correct operational sentence spoken in this entire two-filing arc, and it was whispered by a man lying in a dust duct, and the archive has given it its own line in the notable features because Waluigi SAID SO. Careful. Noise might draw attention. The entire studio arc in seven words. Frame it — and when Waluigi says frame it, he means the archive will be checking the bronze budget at year's end. WAH.

Ahead of them: a faint blue light.

And here is where Waluigi tells you what a commentator does with a blue light, because the last filing taught us all what colored lights mean in this place. A blue light is not a blue light. A blue light is a plot, wearing a bulb. Waluigi has a whole taxonomy now, and every entry is a trap wearing a lamp. The account crawled toward it, and Waluigi crawled after it in spirit, and what was under the light is the single best thing anybody found in this building, and Waluigi includes the churro stick from the previous filing in that ranking. Only just. But he includes it.

sections.heading: Luigi Is Alive, Alone, And Doing MY Job Better Than ME
sections.body:
The vent opened over a maintenance room with a working computer screen, and below it someone was typing fast, muttering *come on… come ON…*

It was Luigi.

ALIVE. The account is exact and Waluigi is going to be exact right back: alive, alone, his face lit blue, exhausted but unharmed. The promo account ended with Luigi missing during a strange tape, and Waluigi filed that loss, and the correction kept it, and NOW — one ceiling vent later — the man is sitting at a terminal two rooms from the fight, running his own investigation.

Look at his desk, because the desk is the story. Security camera feeds. A map of the studio. And notes headed **Wario's corruption.**

Notes. On Wario. The brother of the most famous missing man in the world sat down inside the thing that took his brother and started building a FILE. He typed that he had to find Mario. He typed that he had to fix this. A scared brother running his own investigation with better tools than this archive has ever had, and nobody to tell. Waluigi has run this archive for years on less, and he is NOT proud of how the comparison comes out.

Waluigi has complicated feelings and he is going to file all of them. Pride: that is a MARSHKEEPER-grade work ethic and Luigi does not even work here. Envy: the archive has been chasing the Mario disappearance with newspaper clippings and a charred note, and Luigi walked in and got security feeds, a MAP, and a corruption file. Alarm: because the maintenance computer is the best evidence this case has ever been handed, and it is sitting in a building that RESETS ITS OWN ROOMS, which means the file is a candle in a house fire.

And caution — because the archive has already filed one Luigi that was not Luigi. The blue Luigi. The lava bridge. Waluigi has a whole shelf of things that wore a friendly face, and Darian — watching from the vent, shushing his own steward — said *let's see if he does anything rash; we don't know how dangerous he is.* That is the CORRECT instinct in this building and Waluigi has said so in ink and he will say it again here in a bigger font: VERIFY FIRST. Waluigi said it yesterday about a different brother. The ink is barely DRY. The man at the blue light zoomed cameras, checked door sensors, typed notes, seemed normal.

And then he grabbed a flashlight and stood up to leave. Hold that too. Everything in this filing is a held object that goes off later. Waluigi told you to hold it. He holds things for a living.

sections.heading: The Steward Stops The Kill Shot, Which Is Either Treason Or The Best Staff Work Of The Era
sections.body:
Luigi stood up to leave, and Darian went for the drop. Out of the vent, rolling pin coming down on the head of a man he had decided not to trust.

And Alistair's hand closed on his arm MID-SWING.

Stop the film right there, because Waluigi needs a moment with this. A steward grabbed his king's weapon arm. In the Dark Shores that is probably a hanging offense. In Waluigi's archive it is a PROMOTION. In this maintenance room it is the best decision anybody made all night, and Waluigi has a list, and the list includes ordering a V formation out loud like a general.

The steward stopped his own lord's kill shot on a HUNCH. And the hunch was right — and the account, which Waluigi salutes, also records that it was nearly fatal for everybody. Because Luigi turned, saw an armed stranger descending from his ceiling, and did exactly what a cornered man does. He dodged the second swing and put the flashlight into Darian's shoulder hard enough to numb it. Waluigi has taken a hit like that. It ends the argument.

Alistair shouted that they were not here to hurt him. Luigi was not listening. Full panic, ready to fight or flee or scream — and Waluigi notes, quietly, that this is the most REAL Luigi has ever looked in this entire arc. The copies are calm. The brother is terrified. The archive's whole verification crisis, resolved by a flashlight: terror is hard to fake and this building has never once bothered to try.

*WAH! Two minutes of surveillance undone by one rolling pin.* Waluigi wrote that in the margin of the account and he is keeping it there. Two minutes of perfect instinct — watch, verify, shush the steward — spent in one swing of kitchenware. And in the margin, right beside it, the archive's other margin note: the steward earns his keep TWICE in this filing, and the second time is not this.

The second time involves a window. And a flaming pipe. Waluigi is getting there. Do not rush me — the account did not rush, and the account is a machine for teaching patience, which is a strange quality in something that also turns fights into musical numbers.

sections.heading: The Door Comes Off Its Hinges, And A Man Reading A Seating Chart Walks In
sections.body:
The door went off its hinges.

Evil Mario stood in it — bruised, grinning, glowing red-eyed, fresh from beating the real Mario somewhere out in the corridors. And he looked around the room, and the account gives him the line, and Waluigi gives him the line again because it is the most revealing thing the copy ever said: *Innocence doesn't get you far.*

Innocence doesn't get you far. That is not a threat, Waluigi has heard threats, Waluigi has FILED threats. That is a POLICY STATEMENT. Waluigi has read policy statements before, and this one has MANAGEMENT written all over it. That is a man quoting the employee handbook of whatever this place is. Hold it — it comes back at the end of the filing with a whole different accent.

Three against one, Darian counted. *We can take him… I think.*

They could not. The account is honest about the arithmetic in a way Waluigi respects: Evil Mario moved like a special effect. Dodged the flashlight. Dodged the rolling pin. Shoved Alistair into a desk. Laughed the whole time — the account says he laughed the WHOLE time, and Waluigi believes it, because this thing has never once fought like it was in danger, and the end of this filing is going to explain exactly why. He hurled Luigi into a shelf by the collar.

What actually landed was Darian's rolling pin. A full swing. **CLANG.** Into the shoulder. The first honest hit anyone has put on this thing in two filings — two FILINGS, remember, fireballs and javelins and warhammers have all missed this copy — and the weapon that connects is BAKERY EQUIPMENT, wielded by a provincial lord, and Evil Mario grunted and stumbled back, and for one second the room believed. Waluigi believed too. The archive records its weak moments.

They pressed it. Luigi kicked his legs. Alistair, battered upright, called *GO FOR HIS FACE!* And Darian, somewhere in the noise, produced the sentence Waluigi will now have to live with:

**"A king cannot let his subjects fall!"**

The lord and his steward hit the corrupted Mario together and put him through the computer desk. Monitors shattered. And Waluigi will admit the lower-case truth under the capitals: it worked. The king who said his subjects could not fall, and the steward who catches arms mid-swing, put a special effect through a desk with their combined weight, and for one entire second, the filing believed with them.

sections.heading: The Cape Is The Power Source, And The Studio Has A Rescue Squad On Payroll
sections.body:
And then the floor began to shake, and Evil Mario started to laugh again, and standing up out of the wreckage, he wore a cape.

Not a costume cape. The account is specific and Waluigi is going to be specific with it: a cape of shadowy, pixelated feathers, moving unnaturally, like a living thing. And the shaking, the flickering lights, the cracking walls — the shaking was coming FROM it. The cape was the power source.

Waluigi wants that sentence studied. Not the man. The OUTFIT. Everything this filing has fought — two filings of a corrupted Mario who dodges like a special effect — and the engine of it was a garment. Luigi said it out loud, because Luigi has been reading the room correctly all night: his weakness, it has to be. Destroy the cape. Luigi said it and Waluigi seconded it from the future.

Then the floor fell in.

All three of them dropped into the collapse — and three paratroopas in studio uniforms, with parachutes, caught them by the arms out of the air. Studio crew. Parachute rigs. One of them yelled *HOLD ON TIGHT.*

*WAH!* Waluigi has QUESTIONS and he put every one of them in the investigation file, starting with: since when does a television studio keep a paratroopa rescue squad, and WHO WROTE THEM INTO THE BUDGET? Waluigi asked that out loud at his own desk. Nobody answered. Nobody ever answers. You cannot staff a rapid-deployment parachute team on the same books as a coffee machine that lies about being an exit. Unless — and Waluigi is just going to leave this on the table — unless the budget is not a budget, and the crew is not crew, and somebody further up the call sheet rents both by the hour.

Because look at what the squad did next. They did not fly the party out. There is no OUT in this building; the filing has established this with a coffee machine, and Waluigi checked the exits so you do not have to. There are NONE. They flew the party AT Evil Mario. A flying squad in formation, weapons drawn, non-lethal rounds aimed at the cape. *NEUTRALIZE THE THREAT.* The rescue and the attack were the same maneuver, rehearsed, on standby, deployed the moment the floor gave — which means somebody knew the floor would give, and had a choreographed response READY.

And then, with the squad in the air and the target painted, the studio turned the music on.

The studio. Turned the music. ON. Waluigi has been in show business adjacent circles his whole career and he has never once been handed a soundtrack in the middle of a rescue. Hold the beat, readers. The next section has a melody, and I am NOT going to apologize for it.

sections.heading: Plumber Man: The Copy Fights To The Beat Of A Song That Belongs To The Original
sections.body:
**Plumber Man.**

The song is filed in full in the songbook, lyrics exactly as sung, because what happened next cannot be filed without it, and Waluigi means that as a technical statement about EVIDENCE, not as a joke. The studio turned the music on, and Evil Mario began to fight to the beat.

Dodging on the downbeat. Backflips on the chorus. A villain in a feather cape dancing through a tranq barrage in perfect time, while the paratroopas — who train for many things, the account says, and Waluigi has MET some of them now — could not get their timing to land. The copy was not fighting. The copy was PERFORMING. The fight was a NUMBER. Waluigi has seen numbers; the account still calls it a fight, and Waluigi keeps the account's wording, because the account was THERE and Waluigi was not. The number had a soundtrack, and the soundtrack was provided by the venue, and the venue was aiming at its own performer, and NOTHING about that sentence chain is an accident. Waluigi has re-read that chain four times. It does not improve.

And then the song did the one thing the studio did not plan for: it found Luigi.

Luigi covered his ears. And then he STOPPED covering them. He knew the song. He hummed it — weakly, unwillingly, drawn to it — and the account reaches the conclusion the archive also reached, and Waluigi is going to reach it again, slowly, because it is the emotional center of this whole filing: **the song belongs to the real Mario.**

Read the lyrics the way Waluigi just read them. Four feet ten. The stache. The star that powers him. The pipes. The lass. The kingdom. It is a love song disguised as a jingle, and every word of it is TRUE about a man who is currently bleeding somewhere in this building's corridors — and the corrupted copy of that man was using it as a WEAPON, in front of that man's brother, who could not stop humming along. Waluigi cannot hear this song now without filing a complaint about it.

The studio did not just steal a fight. It stole the fight's MEANING and played it back with the moral removed. Waluigi has heard of sampling. This is DESECRATION with a drum track.

At the final note, Mario appeared behind him. Bruised. Hat askew. Crawled out of the wreckage on his own — nobody rescued him either, notice, the rescue squad had OTHER ORDERS. The paratroopas gasped *Sir, you're alive.* Luigi nearly wept. And the real and the corrupted stood face to face while the song faded, and Waluigi will tell you what that staging is, because staging is the word this whole filing has been teaching us: it is a LIGHTING CUE. The hero enters on the final note. Somebody scored the reveal.

sections.heading: A King Orders A V Formation, A Brother Takes The Cape, And A Steward Comes Back Stupid
sections.body:
Four against one now — *still not scared,* Evil Mario said, and cracked his neck, and the fight resumed. Darian ordered the charge — and Evil Mario STOPPED. Mid-motion. Head tilted, eyes flickering like a screen losing signal, the cape's dark feathers starting to fray. A gust came off it that knocked papers, equipment, and finally Alistair — Alistair, who whispered the sentence of the year about noise — clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway like a ragdoll. Waluigi filed a steward MISSING at that point in the account. The filing was premature. It usually is, with Alistair.

The paratroopas caught Luigi and Darian by the arms and anchored to a broken pipe. And then the statue came back to life and hit the real Mario across the face hard enough to put him through a wall, and it was clear the fight was lost.

Until the lord of the Dark Shores remembered what he is FOR.

**"As a king, I order the troops into formation — a V, like a bird."**

Waluigi has read a great many battlefield orders in this archive. A provincial king, standing in a collapsing studio, ordering a paratroopa parachute squadron into a V formation like migratory birds, is now Waluigi's favorite, and the competition includes a centaur declaring a legal argument against the Iron Legion. The squad SNAPPED into the V. The V cut the wind. And on the next order — *grab Luigi, fly him into that cape* — the lead paratroopa took Luigi into the formation's dive, straight at the fraying feathers.

And Luigi — who came to this studio to find his brother, who hummed his brother's song against his own will, who was thrown into a shelf by this thing not twenty minutes ago — reached out with BOTH HANDS and yanked the cape off.

Evil Mario screamed. And Waluigi notes — carefully, in the margin, underlined — that it is the first sound the copy made all night that Waluigi believes was NOT in the script.

The scream became a smile, because this thing has a costume rack, and the account knows it now: in his hand, a tanuki leaf. The transformation ran through him — fox tail, Wario's wild hair, and then, grotesque on his shoulder, a SECOND HEAD. Wario's. Grinning. Waluigi has filed haunted mirrors, vampire invitations, and a spider the size of a school, and a spare WARIO HEAD sprouting off a corrupted Mario's shoulder is still the single most upsetting accessory in the case file.

And through the broken window behind them came Alistair. Blown away minutes ago. Presumed lost. Crashing back in covered in dust, carrying a FLAMING PIPE, with visible rage, executing a plan his own lord described — accurately, in the account, in the lord's OWN WORDS — as *really stupid.* The Wario head popped off like a balloon and burst into smoke, as if it agreed with the assessment. The flaming pipe met the tanuki tail. The leaf caught fire. Mario tackled the thing off its feet, and Luigi snatched the burning leaf out of the air just as it fully ignited.

The steward earns his keep TWICE. Told you. Waluigi keeps score; it is what archivists do instead of sleeping. WAH.

sections.heading: Fire, Water, Ice — And Then A Provincial Lord Says The One Word The Building Obeys
sections.body:
The corrupted Mario ran out of forms to wear and put on the last one. He erupted into fire — no shape left, a living blaze, the room catching around him.

And Darian went for the fire alarm. Found one — red, smashed-glass, by the shattered door — and went for it through the heat ON HIS BELLY, because the flame whip was overhead, saying *it's too risky, but I must keep going.* Debris under his hands. The whip missing him by inches. He smashed the glass and pulled the handle.

Sprinklers. Water everywhere. The fire form hissed, shrank, flickered. And Darian looked at his hands — soot, scratches, small burns — and the account gives him one word of inventory: ALIVE.

And then Evil Mario pointed at the dying fire, and the room turned COLD. Frost climbed the walls. Breath turned visible. The sprinkler water became icicles, and the corrupted Mario stood remade as a body of shimmering blue ice with glowing eyes. The real Mario punched it and his fist froze STUCK in the surface. Waluigi has filed weapons that break. This is the first weapon that got a RECEIPT.

*How many forms does this thing have?* Darian said. And then answered himself: **this must be all an act.**

The ice sculpture smirked.

Which is how they knew he was right. Waluigi wants that beat preserved exactly as the account timed it, because it is the moment the entire two-filing arc changes genre: the monster is caught SMIRKING at its own review. Waluigi has been smirked at by professionals. This was a CURTAIN CALL. It is not a beast wearing shapes. It is a PERFORMER wearing forms, and a performer can be directed, and anything that can be directed has a director, and the room was about to meet him.

But first, the word. The filing exists for the word. Darian — burned, numb-shouldered, rolling pin in hand, standing in falling sprinkler water with the ice mid-advance — said:

**"CUT!"**

Everything stopped. Waluigi has checked the audio on that word. It is one syllable, and it beat ice. The ice stopped spreading. The paratroopas lowered their weapons mid-breath. The real Mario lowered his fists *like he just remembered something* — that phrase is the account's and Waluigi is keeping it, it is the best stage direction in the archive — and Evil Mario's frozen expression flickered, pixelated, broke apart like a bad signal. The word had reached whatever was running the show, and whatever was running the show FLINCHED.

Theatrical curtains came down from the whole ceiling. Crew voices. Someone shouting *cut the feed.* The curtains closed with a THUD, and when they opened again the studio had reset itself: the original break room, no flames, no ice, no evil copies. *What just happened?* Mario asked. Nobody had it.

Waluigi has re-shelved half of this file accordingly. The question is no longer how to beat Evil Mario. The question is WHO IS AFRAID OF THE WORD CUT, AND WHY. A trap cannot be embarrassed. A STAGE can. Waluigi moved this file from the TRAPS shelf to the THEATRE shelf tonight; the label maker is still warm.

sections.heading: The Applause Was For NOBODY, And Waluigi Cannot Put That Sentence Down
sections.body:
Wario walked in clapping, and applause came out of the dark.

*Bravo! What an entertaining performance!* Oscar-worthy, he said. The ice scene — brilliant special effects. And an audience that WAS NOT THERE roared approval while a television on the wall replayed the fight as security footage. He admitted ALL of it with his arms spread: *Best show on TV!* And then, the one true sentence a producer has ever said in this archive: some of you didn't sign up for it.

The real Mario asked the only question that mattered. *You used me? Like some kind of puppet?* And Wario waved it off as a bit of fun — and Waluigi notes the WAVE, because the wave is a man who has never once been asked to account for anything and has developed the reflexes of somebody who never will be.

And Darian — who has spent two filings, ONE DAY, learning to check this building's work — looked at the audience.

**Every seat was empty.**

Read it again. Waluigi has read it several times and it has not gotten lighter. He checks it every pass, like a tooth. Still not lighter. Beyond the seats, through the windows, the whole studio facility: silent. No crew. No life. Nobody. The applause was a RECORDING for a room of chairs. Waluigi has stood in empty rooms before. They at least had the decency to be QUIET about it. The show has an audience the way the coffee machine has an exit: on paper, in spirit, and NOT IN THE ROOM.

*We're alone,* Mario said. And Wario's smirk finally faltered — and four men who had just survived his variety hour began to close on him with their sleeves rolled.

The empty seats are the part Waluigi cannot file yet, and he told you so in the assessment and he will tell you again on the track: a show needs an audience. The applause track says one exists. The room says it does not. Either the audience is somewhere the windows do not show, or the performance is being recorded for a viewer the building is not prepared to name. BOTH readings have a person at the end of them. And Waluigi has a name he is not writing down until he has to.

He is not writing it down. He is, however, writing down the sleeve-rolling, because four survivors squaring up at their producer is the most honest television this studio has produced all day. Waluigi would watch THAT show. He would rate it highly.

sections.heading: The Man Wario Bows To, And The Small Wired Thing That Runs Everything
sections.body:
They never got to him. A voice behind them said, *since this was all for show, let's see how you like the real deal* — and there stood a figure in a director's cap, holding a script.

And Wario — the showman, the Apparition, the boss of everyone visible, the man who just called this the best show on TV — went PALE. And BOWED. And said: *Boss.* One word. Waluigi has filed confessions longer than that syllable, and none of them were more total.

**Director Mario.** Waluigi is filing that name exactly as the account gives it, cold, calculating, no warmth in him anywhere, and the account's own ledger of the last hour snaps into focus like a focus pull, which is what it was ALL ALONG: the corrupted Mario was an ACTOR. The song was a NUMBER. Wario was the PRODUCER. And the applause, the exits, the reset break room — that was the VENUE, and venues have owners. Waluigi has been asking who profits since the newspaper clipping, and the profit wears a CAP now.

The Director said the show had gone over better than Wario knew. He knew about the results. And then he said the quiet part with his cigar snapping in half in his fingers, and the account censors it and Waluigi will censor it too, because this is a family archive: *you tried to f*** me.*

He took Wario by the collar and put him through a wall hard enough to shake the building. *You betrayed me — you ruined MY show.* One punch, and Wario was unconscious. And then the detail Waluigi files above even the wall: he straightened his SUIT. Like a man who has swatted a fly. He looked once at Darian, Alistair, Luigi, and the real Mario — UNREADABLY — and walked out without a word. Waluigi has met that silence once or twice. It is the silence of a man who does not rate the meeting.

But the account has one more reel, and it is the reel the whole case turns on. Darian — ALONE — noticed that Evil Mario was still there. Half in shadow. Perfectly still. Red eyes tracking the Director to the door. He told NOBODY. He signalled Alistair. He let the room arrive at its own stillness around the thing in the corner. And Evil Mario smiled, slowly, and raised ONE FINGER, and pointed — not at any of them — at the door the Director had left through.

The actor pointed at the man who directs him. Waluigi has waited two filings for a witness to point at SOMETHING. Remember when Waluigi said the *innocence* line was a policy statement? The policy has a SIGNATORY.

Darian stepped into the dim hallway and hid in a dark alcove, and the Director walked past him close enough to TOUCH. In one hand: a folder. In the other, carried with the ease of long habit, a small remote device with buttons and wires running from it. A control unit. For Evil Mario — or for the whole studio. Waluigi has wanted an OBJECT for this case since a charred note on a doorstep. The case finally HAS one.

The account ends on the thought the archive now cannot put down: that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.

The recommendation, one more time, from the commentary desk: the REMOTE, before the Director notices it was seen. And somebody collect Luigi's notes on the way out. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.

WAH.
